identity.name: Vingt-8 ISO
identity.one_liner: The Vingt-8 ISO keeps Voutilainen's calibre 28 and its double-wheel direct-impulse escapement, then breaks the one rule the dial exists to keep: the minute hand turns thirteen times an hour instead of once, so reading the time stops being reflex and starts being a decision.

comps.condition: Phillips New York Watch Auction: XIV, lot 140. Circa 2017, 18k white gold, movement no. 28ISO-2, in-house cal. 28 with 35 jewels, 39mm. Phillips records this as likely the second Vingt-8 ISO ever made and the second offered by the house. Hammer USD 950,000; sold price is hammer plus the 27% buyer's premium. Certificate booklet dated February 2017, fitted box, extra crocodile strap.

provenance_events.description: Kari Voutilainen introduces the Vingt-8 ISO, an offbeat reinterpretation of his 2011 flagship. Phillips records that the rotating display required a newly configured movement, slightly thicker than the standard calibre 28.

The Phillips lot offered in New York in June 2026 carries a Voutilainen certificate booklet dated February 2017 and movement number 28ISO-2, which Phillips reads as likely the second ISO Voutilainen built. The watch was fresh to the auction market.

provenance_events.person_or_event: Phillips New York Watch Auction: XIV, lot 140
provenance_events.description: The Vingt-8 ISO offered as lot 140 sold for USD 1,206,500 against an estimate of USD 100,000-200,000, after 20 bids. The over-estimate reflects the reference's standing rather than its condition; Phillips describes the dial as pristine and the case as unpolished.

narrative.story:
Every watch hands you the time for free. The Vingt-8 ISO is the rare one that charges for it. Kari Voutilainen took the thinking behind Daniel Kahneman's two-system model of the mind - System 1 doing something without effort, System 2 doing something that requires thought - and built it into a movement. The hour hand turns once every twelve hours as it always should. The minute hand turns thirteen times an hour instead of once. On the hour the two hands lie on top of each other; at the half hour they sit exactly opposite; at the quarter hours they are ninety degrees apart. Nothing is hidden and nothing is broken. The wearer simply cannot read it without deciding to read it.

The mechanics are Voutilainen's own. The calibre 28 is the movement he designed to carry the company after 2011, built around a double-wheel direct-impulse escapement: two escape wheels push the balance directly, with no lever and no lubricating oil on the escapement. The balance is oversized at 13.6mm and free-sprung, carrying rose-gold regulating weights, and its spring mixes a Breguet overcoil on the outside with the little-known Grossmann curve on the inside. The ISO needed a reconfigured, slightly thicker movement to drive its rotating chapter ring, and the watch Phillips sold in New York in June 2026 carried 35 jewels.

That sale is also the argument about how scarce this is. The watch was the second ISO Phillips has ever offered, and the movement number 28ISO-2 indicates it is likely the second one Voutilainen made. It carried an estimate of USD 100,000 to 200,000 and made USD 1,206,500. Voutilainen completed 67 watches in total across 2021 with roughly thirty people on the bench.
narrative.collector_notes: There is no public retail price for the ISO. Voutilainen sells a small number of pieces a year and does not publish a list, so this register carries an empty MSRP history rather than a borrowed one. The only sale on file is the Phillips New York lot. An enlarged 44mm ISO in rose gold exists as a unique piece, but that is a bespoke one-off and is not the same reference.
